child._comment: W_C — THE INTERNET (the network of networks, running TCP/IP). The trunk node, and — like Manhattan and unlike QG — it is SOLID (the crown is not hollow). NOT the ARPANET (that is a parent-substrate); the CHILD is the internetworking layer that lets HETEROGENEOUS, independently-owned networks interconnect with no central control. The thing born in this merge is the open, end-to-end, network-of-networks ARCHITECTURE — which is why the WEB, e-commerce and social media are harvest (descendants), not the child.
child.name: The Internet (TCP/IP — the network of networks)
child.kernel: A global, decentralized network-of-networks: independently-owned heterogeneous packet networks interconnected through gateways/routers by a common protocol suite (TCP/IP), under the open-architecture principle (each network stands on its own, no internal change required to join) and the end-to-end principle (intelligence at the hosts, not in the network). CRUCIAL contrast with QG's kernel: this is a description of an EXISTING, deployed object (billions of hosts; the substrate of the world economy), not a specification of a sought target. CRUCIAL contrast with the ARPANET: the child is NOT a single packet network but the INTERNETWORKING layer that federates many.
child._frame_note: knowledge (the protocol architecture), space+time (a planet-spanning infrastructure built over ~3 decades), and a real {meaning} engagement: the Internet became a moral/political object (the 'two visions' of standardization — decentralized open process vs centralized state/PTT control; later net-neutrality, surveillance, platform power). The meaning-frame engagement here is for 'WHO governs the network and by what process' (the protocol wars as a power struggle), echoing QG's meaning-frame 'which child is winning' and Manhattan's 'was the child's use justified'.

utility._comment: Pav's three utility legs. Like Manhattan (and unlike QG's largely-prospective utility), the utility is overwhelmingly REALIZED.
utility.unifier: Fused two previously-separate wrappers — single-network packet-switching + the open-architecture internetworking principle — into one operational system that UNIFIES all prior heterogeneous networks (ARPANET, SATNET, PRNET, Ethernet LANs, X.25 publics, later cellular) under one address+transport scheme, AND became the universal substrate the Web, e-commerce, the cloud and social media all sit on. passesW_CTest: YES — the network-of-networks is genuinely unreachable from either parent alone: packet-switching alone yields ISOLATED single networks (the ARPANET, NPL, CYCLADES, X.25 publics — each a silo); the open-architecture/end-to-end PRINCIPLE alone is an empty design stance with nothing to connect. Only TOGETHER do they yield a federating internetwork.
utility.compressor: QUALITATIVE ONLY (no fabricated bits). TCP/IP 'compresses' the entire heterogeneity of the world's networks into one thin waist ('IP on everything' — Cerf's 1992 slogan): every application above and every link-layer below need know only the narrow IP datagram interface (the hourglass/narrow-waist architecture). It also compresses 'how to add a new network' into a single rule (run IP at the gateway), distinct from QG's PRINCIPLED-null compressor: here the compression is REAL but still assessed qualitatively (MDL-in-bits needs latent embeddings — a later step).

weld._comment: The merge: parents -> child. THE HEART OF THE SPECIMEN. Here the weld is a CONSUMMATED, institution-cascade-welded, exogenously-forced merge whose distinctive feature (vs Manhattan) is that consummation ran through a RIVAL-STANDARD WAR. The clean 2-parent diagram (packet-switching x internetworking) is present and faithful as a projection, but (R1/R27) the welding agent is NEITHER parent: it is an ORDERED CASCADE of mediating institutions (ARPA -> IPTO -> BBN -> universities-under-contract -> INWG -> IAB/IETF -> ISOC), with the human welders (Cerf & Kahn) sitting a layer up from both packet-switching and the open-architecture stance. See mediating_wrapper and discrepancies.

parents.name: Packet-switching (distributed, survivable, store-and-forward data networking)
parents.kernel: The technique of chopping messages into addressed blocks (packets) and routing them independently, store-and-forward, over a decentralized mesh: Baran's distributed-adaptive-message-block / survivable-network design at RAND (1959-64, 'On Distributed Communications'); Davies' independent NPL invention that COINED 'packet' (1965-66); Kleinrock's queueing theory; realized in the ARPANET (BBN's IMPs, 1969) and the NPL network (1970). The technology that makes data networking efficient and robust. frame {knowledge}.
parents._parent_kind_note: (R4) the CONTENT parent — the core networking technology. Itself multiply-rooted + priority-disputed (Baran/Davies/Kleinrock); see parents_full + discrepancies.

parents.name: Open-architecture internetworking (the network-of-networks principle)
parents.kernel: Kahn's open-architecture stance (1973): connect INDEPENDENTLY-OWNED, heterogeneous networks with no internal change required to any of them, via gateways, with reliability pushed to the end hosts (the end-to-end principle) and a connectionless datagram core (Pouzin's CYCLADES contribution). The design philosophy + the datagram + the end-to-end principle that turn many isolated packet networks into ONE internetwork. frame {knowledge, meaning}.

The D5 graded-membership signature, milder than Manhattan's 0.6 war-state because internetworking is a more coherent single idea than 'the war-state'.

parents_full.name: Baran's distributed/survivable packet network (RAND, 1959-64)
parents_full.kernel: Distributed-adaptive-message-block 'hot-potato' store-and-forward routing over a survivable mesh, motivated by surviving a nuclear first strike ('On Distributed Communications', RAND P-2626 1962 / RM-3420 1964). The survivability + distributed-routing root of W_A.

parents_full.name: Davies' NPL packet-switching (1965-66)
parents_full.kernel: Independent invention of packet-switching at the National Physical Laboratory; COINED the word 'packet'; proposed a UK national data network; built the NPL network (1970). The civil/commercial root of W_A (and the term itself).

parents_full.name: Kleinrock's queueing theory of message/packet networks
parents_full.kernel: Doctoral queueing-theoretic analysis of message-switched networks (1961-62, book 1964); later analytic work on the ARPANET. CONTESTED as a packet-switching origin (Davies/Baran/Taylor dispute the claim) — recorded as a parent at reduced confidence + a priority-dispute discrepancy.
parents_full._confidence_note: 0.6, NOT because the queueing-theory work is doubtful (it is real and load-bearing for ARPANET performance) but because the CLAIM that it ORIGINATED packet-switching is contested (Davies 2001: 'I can find no evidence that he understood the principles of packet switching'; McKenzie: 'nothing in the entire 1964 book...alludes to the idea of packetization'; Kleinrock 2023 acknowledged the early work was about MESSAGE switching). Graded membership as a PARENT.

parents_full.name: Kahn's open-architecture principle (1973)
parents_full.kernel: The four ground rules: each network stands on its own; no internal change required to connect; best-effort with end-host recovery; no global control. The architectural stance that defines W_B.

parents_full.name: Pouzin's datagram / connectionless model (CYCLADES, early 1970s)
parents_full.kernel: The CONNECTIONLESS datagram (Pouzin coined 'datagram'); CYCLADES was the first to push reliable delivery to the END HOSTS rather than the network. Cerf & Kahn explicitly acknowledged CYCLADES in the 1974 paper; Gerard Le Lann carried the concepts into the Transmission Control Program. The datagram leg of W_B.
parents_full._parent_kind_note: (R4) borderline content/method — the datagram is a concrete construct (content) embodying the end-to-end stance (method). Load-bearing AND a dormancy/forcing story in its own right (CYCLADES was defunded — see forcing_events + R29).

parents_full.name: The end-to-end principle (Saltzer-Reed-Clark, articulated 1981)
parents_full.kernel: Put function at the endpoints, keep the network simple (the design rationale later articulated formally in 'End-to-End Arguments in System Design', 1981/84). Present in practice in CYCLADES/TCP from the early 1970s; the principle that justifies the thin-waist architecture. The methodological spine of W_B.

weld.shared_sub_object_S: S = the GATEWAY/DATAGRAM INTERCONNECTION POINT at the exact place where the PACKET-SWITCHING technique (efficient routing WITHIN a network) meets the OPEN-ARCHITECTURE requirement to join INDEPENDENT networks WITHOUT a common owner or internal change. Three faces: (1) the GATEWAY (later 'router') — the box that sits BETWEEN networks and forwards datagrams across the boundary (the literal seam, Cerf-Kahn 1974); (2) the COMMON DATAGRAM FORMAT (IP) — a single address+packet format every network agrees to carry, embodying the narrow waist; (3) the END-TO-END principle — reliability lives at the hosts, so the heterogeneous, unreliable networks in the middle need not be changed. Genuine overlap, not a pile: packet-switching owns intra-network routing, open-architecture owns the no-central-control federation, and ONLY at the gateway+datagram do they fuse into an internetwork.
weld._shared_sub_object_S_note: HIGH confidence the seam is genuine. Contrast QG (direction-of-weld disputed) and Darwin+Mendel (fractured S): here S is multi-faceted but AGREED among the Internet engineers. The CONTEST at the seam is EXTERNAL — the rival OSI/X.25 camps proposed a DIFFERENT seam (virtual circuits + strict layering + connection-oriented network service), which is the protocol-wars discrepancy, NOT an internal fracture of THIS S.

weld.surprise: The genuine JOINT-surprise (reachable only from BOTH parents) is NOT that a data network exists — single packet networks (the ARPANET, NPL, CYCLADES, the X.25 publics) were implied by packet-switching ALONE (W_A). The genuine joint-surprise is INTERNETWORKING: that INDEPENDENTLY-OWNED, HETEROGENEOUS, MUTUALLY-DISTRUSTING networks could be federated into one seamless whole with NO central control, NO common owner, and NO internal change to any member network — and that this open, end-to-end, 'dumb-network/smart-edges' architecture would SCALE to a planet and outcompete every centrally-planned alternative. Neither parent predicts this alone: packet-switching alone yields SILOS (each network a walled garden); the open-architecture PRINCIPLE alone is an empty stance with nothing to connect. STANDOUT SUB-SURPRISE: the winning architecture was the LESS-CONTROLLED one — the camp with no central authority, no government mandate, and 'rough consensus and running code' beat the camp (OSI/X.25) backed by ISO, the CCITT, the PTTs and government procurement mandates (GOSIP). The PHANTOM here (cf. Manhattan's phantom enemy): the heavily-funded, officially-mandated OSI stack was widely believed INEVITABLE ('OSI is now inevitable' — Metcalfe 1989) and never shipped at scale — a real institutional force defeated by a child it had dismissed. META-SURPRISE: a consummated weld can be carried to global victory NOT by the best-funded mediating institutions but by the FASTEST-ITERATING, least-governed ones — and a rival lineage's STATE BACKING can be the very thing that SLOWS it (OSI's committee process; CYCLADES killed by its own PTT in favor of Minitel).

surprise_priority.first_conjectured_by: J.C.R. Licklider ('Intergalactic Computer Network' memos, IPTO)

weld.bits_note: QUALITATIVE ONLY. Distinct from QG's PRINCIPLED-null (QG could not be MDL-scored because the child did not exist); here the child exists, so the compression is real, but it is still assessed QUALITATIVELY (MDL-in-bits needs latent embeddings — a later step). survived: Packet-switching itself (Baran/Davies) — survived as the core transport of every Internet link.
The DATAGRAM / connectionless model (Pouzin/CYCLADES) — survived as IP, defeating the rival virtual-circuit model (X.25/OSI CONS).
The END-TO-END principle (CYCLADES->TCP; Saltzer-Reed-Clark 1981) — survived as the Internet's defining architectural commitment.
Baran's distributed/no-central-control survivability — survived as the Internet's decentralization and its governance ethos.
The RFC / 'rough consensus and running code' open-process method (Crocker 1969; Clark 1992) — survived as the IETF's standardization culture.

OSI's STRICT SEVEN-LAYER model + connection-oriented network service — DROPPED/defeated (TCP/IP's looser four-layer + connectionless IP won the protocol wars).

dormancy_intervals._why_frame_comment: (R11) PHYSICAL/POLITICAL — a state/PTT funding-and-policy decision killed the network (echoing QG/Bronstein's physical-frame squeeze and Keynesian's neoliberal-movement squeeze, NOT a theorem). phase_trajectory.note: Packet-switching (Baran/Davies) and the internetworking VISION (Licklider's Intergalactic Network) develop in COMPLEMENTARITY — independent but mutually-needy. See pre_weld_relationship (the single home for the relationship strength).

Kahn's open-architecture problem (1973) + the Cerf-Kahn paper (May 1974) DRAW the internetworking weld as a low-confidence conjecture. RFC 675 (Dec 1974) names 'Internet'. Indexes sw-cerf-kahn + surprise_priority.

A ~9-year DISTRIBUTED welding phase (NOT Manhattan's ultra-fast 33 months): TCP/IP split (1978), the INWG fork (1976), UNIX/BSD shipping TCP/IP (1983), refinement via the RFC process. The longest non-frontier welding(process) phase in the batch. Indexes sub_welds + the cascade.
The NCP->TCP/IP flag day consummates the weld operationally; NSFNET (1986) scales it. Indexes sw-flag-day + sw-nsfnet.

phase_trajectory.note: A distinctive RIVAL-WAR phase: TCP/IP fights OSI + X.25 for ~a decade and wins (~1990-95). This phase is where the rival-lifecycle-coupling (R23) lives — one standard's rise IS another's fall. Indexes sw-protocol-wars-won + the rival relatives + the rival-coupling forcing events.

Commercialization (NSF backbone retired 30 Apr 1995) + the dot-com build-out + mobile/cloud HARDEN the Internet into the global communications baseline. to=null marks an OPEN hardening (still the baseline in 2026) — same 'never-stops-mattering' null as Manhattan's, the OPPOSITE of QG's never-born null.

This is the SINGLE HOME for the relationship strength (the phase_trajectory pre_weld entry marks only WHEN).
pre_weld_relationship.note: Mutually-needy parents: packet-switching held the intra-network transport, open-architecture held the no-central-control federation principle. NOTE: the ANTAGONISM in this specimen is BETWEEN RIVAL LINEAGES (TCP/IP vs OSI/X.25), not between the two PARENTS — a structural difference from Darwin+Mendel (where the parents themselves were antagonists).

All listed types are from the CORE controlled vocabulary (no NEW vocabulary term proposed, so no discrepancy row needed for vocabulary — unlike Keynesian/deep-learning which proposed new terms). The dominant types (mediator-welded + state/funding-mobilized + crisis-pulled) are exactly the cascade/institution/Cold-War features this specimen was chosen to instantiate.

A state/funding-mobilized weld (the 'war' sense is the Cold-War research climate, not a hot war). TRIPLE-attests D2's government-actor finding (with Manhattan + Keynesian).

The Cold-War crisis (Sputnik) PULLED ARPA into existence and funded the whole enterprise; a late DEREGULATION pull (NSF commercialization) accelerated consummation. A milder, slower crisis-pull than Manhattan's (decades, not 33 months) — but the second crisis-pulled instance the batch was seeking.

Enabling instruments: the ARPANET/IMPs (the deployable packet testbed), cheap minicomputers + UNIX/BSD shipping TCP/IP (1983), and later Ethernet LANs + Cisco routers (the gateway-as-product). The instruments made the open-architecture principle deployable at scale.
Fused packet-switching with the open-architecture principle into one operational system that UNIFIES all prior heterogeneous networks under one protocol suite — the classic unifier leg.

roots._comment: DOWN, in the PHYSICAL frame. The recursive descent from W_C toward people and place. Confidence FADES and depth RISES as you go deeper. The ground kernel '(0)' lives in actors[] (kind:individual + agencies/labs/companies), NOT here. The deep frontier roots are the PRIORITY DISPUTE (who invented packet-switching) and the CONTESTED GENEALOGY (what counts as 'the Internet'), which sit in fuzzy_layer.frontier.

sub_wrappers.name: Packet-switching (the technique)
sub_wrappers.kernel: Chop messages into addressed packets, route them independently store-and-forward over a decentralized mesh. Baran (RAND, 1959-64) + Davies (NPL, 1965-66, coined 'packet'), independently.
sub_wrappers.who_called_it: Paul Baran (RAND) + Donald Davies (NPL); Davies coined 'packet'

sub_wrappers.name: Distributed / survivable no-central-control routing
sub_wrappers.kernel: Baran's survivable-network insight: a distributed mesh with redundant paths and no single point of failure (motivated by surviving a nuclear first strike). The decentralization root.

sub_wrappers.name: Queueing theory of networks
sub_wrappers.kernel: Analytic performance theory of message/packet networks (Kleinrock, 1961-64). A METHOD root for sizing/analyzing the network — its CONTESTED status as a packet-switching ORIGIN is a priority dispute, but as an analysis tool it is uncontested.

sub_wrappers.name: The datagram / connectionless model
sub_wrappers.kernel: Pouzin's CYCLADES datagram (early 1970s): a self-contained, independently-routed packet with delivery responsibility at the END HOSTS. The connectionless core that became IP and defeated the virtual-circuit (X.25) rival.

sub_wrappers.name: The open-architecture principle
sub_wrappers.kernel: Kahn's four ground rules (1973): each network stands on its own; no internal change to join; best-effort with end-host recovery; no global control. The federation stance of W_B.

sub_wrappers.name: The end-to-end principle
sub_wrappers.kernel: Function at the endpoints, simple network in the middle (CYCLADES->TCP in practice; articulated formally by Saltzer, Reed & Clark 1981/84). The design rationale for the narrow waist.
sub_wrappers.who_called_it: Jerome Saltzer, David Reed, David Clark (1981); practiced earlier in CYCLADES/TCP

sub_wrappers.name: The RFC / 'rough consensus and running code' open-process method
sub_wrappers.kernel: The Request for Comments genre (Crocker, RFC 1, 1969) + the IETF norm 'we reject kings, presidents and voting; we believe in rough consensus and running code' (Clark 1992). The METHODOLOGICAL root of how the Internet standardizes — and a key reason TCP/IP out-iterated OSI.

sub_wrappers.name: The gateway / router
sub_wrappers.kernel: The box that sits BETWEEN networks and forwards datagrams across the boundary (Cerf-Kahn 1974) — the literal physical embodiment of the seam S; later a commercial product (Cisco). The instrument root.
sub_wrappers.who_called_it: Cerf & Kahn (the concept); Cisco et al. (the product)

harvest._comment: UP, in the LATENT + CULTURAL frame. Like Manhattan (and unlike QG's canopy-over-a-hollow-trunk), here the canopy grows over a SOLID trunk — the harvest is the realized descendant order. All harvest nodes frame_layer: latent by default (D3). The dominant harvest (the Web) is itself a child-of-the-child.

descendants.name: The World Wide Web
descendants.what: Berners-Lee at CERN (1989-91): HTTP/HTML/URLs over TCP/IP; the first website (info.cern.ch) Aug 1991; CERN placed it in the public domain (1993). The dominant harvest application — the Internet's 'killer app' that drove mass adoption and was itself the killer argument that ended the protocol wars.

descendants.name: E-commerce + the platform economy
descendants.what: The dot-com boom and the digital economy — Amazon, eBay, Google, and the entire commercial Internet; the platform business model. The Internet as the substrate of a large fraction of the world economy.

descendants.name: Social media + the networked public sphere
descendants.what: The 2010s social-platform transformation of communication, media and politics — and its pathologies (misinformation, surveillance, platform power, the attention economy). A double-edged harvest.

descendants.name: Cloud computing + the mobile/streaming era
descendants.what: Cloud infrastructure, the smartphone/app ecosystem, streaming media — the Internet as a utility delivered to billions of pocket devices. The infrastructural maturation of the child.

descendants.name: Internet governance + cyber-statecraft
descendants.what: A new domain of statecraft and conflict: ICANN/IETF/ISOC governance, the net-neutrality debates, cyberwar, and the 'splinternet'/digital-sovereignty fragmentation. The 'two visions' meaning-frame conflict, harvested into geopolitics.

cultural_harvest.what: The Internet as the defining infrastructure of the late-20th/early-21st century — 'cyberspace', 'online', 'going viral', the 'information superhighway'; the reorganization of work, commerce, media and social life around being networked. confidence ~0.9.

Cyberpunk and the 'cyberspace' imaginary (Gibson's 'Neuromancer' 1984 coined cyberspace just as the real internetwork consolidated; 'The Matrix' 1999; the metaverse) — fiction running ahead of and feeding back into the real network. confidence ~0.8.

The 'rough consensus and running code' ethos + the open-standards/open-source movement as a reusable cultural template for decentralized, permissionless coordination (later echoed by open-source software, the blockchain/'decentralization' discourse). confidence ~0.8.

relatives._comment: WIDE edges (SCHEMA_v2.md §2.5; still flagged for ratification). THE MOST TELLING RELATIVES here are the RIVAL ARCHITECTURES (OSI, X.25, Minitel/Transpac) — recorded as relation:rival, and the locus of the rival-lifecycle-coupling (R23). NOTE: these rivals are NOT candidate_children of the weld (they are adjacent lineages, not rival outputs of THIS weld's two parents) — the §2.5 relatives layer is exactly where a defeated rival framework belongs (cf. Manhattan's Uranverein, Maxwell's Weber electrodynamics).

edges.name: OSI (Open Systems Interconnection, ISO/CCITT, model published 1984)
edges.note: The PRIMARY RIVAL ARCHITECTURE: a seven-layer, connection-oriented, formally-standardized stack backed by ISO, the CCITT, European governments and US GOSIP procurement mandates. Widely believed INEVITABLE ('OSI is now inevitable' — Metcalfe 1989) and never shipped at scale; defeated by TCP/IP ~1990-95. The locus of the rival-lifecycle-coupling (its mandate-driven rise SQUEEZED TCP/IP; its collapse was TCP/IP's victory) AND the whig-vs-revisionist historiography (Russell: was its defeat inevitable-on-merit or contingent-and-political?). SQUEEZED TCP/IP via GOSIP, then collapsed.

edges.name: X.25 (CCITT virtual-circuit packet standard, 1976) + the public data networks
edges.note: The CONNECTION-ORIENTED (virtual-circuit) rival, championed by the PTTs/telcos and the CCITT (approved 1976). 'The main European data protocol for fifteen to twenty years' (Kirstein). Embodies the OPPOSITE seam to TCP/IP (virtual circuits + network-managed reliability vs datagrams + end-host reliability). Pouzin: the datagram-vs-virtual-circuit fight was 'a power struggle between carriers and the computer industry ... IBM vs Telecommunications'. Declined as IP overtook it (JANET 1991; closed 1997). The rival whose architecture lost even though its backers held the standards bodies.

edges.name: Minitel / Transpac (France's national X.25 network)
edges.note: France's wildly-successful national videotex network over the connection-oriented Transpac (X.25). THE DEEPEST RIVAL-COUPLING IRONY: France's PTT KILLED its own datagram pioneer (CYCLADES, defunded 1978) to back the connection-oriented Minitel/Transpac — and the connectionless datagram principle CYCLADES had pioneered then WON globally as IP, while Minitel itself was eventually shut down (2012, displaced by the Internet). A lineage that suppressed the winning idea at home and lost to it abroad. The single best rival-lifecycle-coupling (R23) datum in the specimen.

edges.name: Proprietary vendor stacks (IBM SNA 1974, DEC DECnet 1975, Xerox XNS)
edges.note: Closed, single-vendor network architectures that pre-dated and competed with open internetworking (by the late 1970s IBM's networking was 'two orders of magnitude larger' than the ARPANET). Defeated/absorbed by TCP/IP's open multi-vendor model. The closed-garden rivals (contrast the open child).

edges.name: The ARPANET (the parent-substrate, decommissioned 1990)
edges.note: NOT the child and not a rival — the PACKET-SWITCHING SUBSTRATE the weld was built on/over (the W_A parent realized). Recorded as relation:influence to keep the genealogy honest: the popular 'ARPANET = the Internet' is a contested-genealogy conflation (the Internet is the internetworking LAYER, the ARPANET one network it federated). The ARPANET was decommissioned 1990; the Internet outgrew it.

fuzzy_layer._comment: The LOD/confidence partition — a DERIVED digest of the per-node memberships (D5). Like Manhattan (and unlike QG's hollow crown), the certain core spans the LOWER, MIDDLE AND CROWN of the tree — a consummated case with a solid trunk all the way up. The frontier is located OFF the main trunk: the PRIORITY DISPUTE (who invented packet-switching), the CONTESTED GENEALOGY (what 'the Internet' is), and the WHIG-VS-REVISIONIST historiography (was TCP/IP's victory inevitable?). The fuzz here is in ATTRIBUTION + HISTORIOGRAPHY (who/why), not in whether the child was born.
certain_core: W_A = packet-switching exists (Baran/Davies, early-mid 1960s) and W_B = the open-architecture/internetworking principle exists (Kahn 1973; Pouzin's datagram) (~0.9-0.93).
The seam S is genuine (gateway + common datagram + end-to-end) (~0.9).
The child EXISTS and works — the Internet is the deployed global network-of-networks running TCP/IP (~0.92).
Cerf-Kahn specified internetworking (May 1974) and the term 'Internet' dates to RFC 675 (Dec 1974) (~0.95).
The 1 Jan 1983 flag day (NCP->TCP/IP) consummated the weld operationally; NSFNET (1986) scaled it; commercialization (1995) hardened it (~0.92-0.95).
The mediating welder is an ORDERED INSTITUTIONAL CASCADE (ARPA->IPTO->BBN->INWG->IETF->NSF->ISOC), NOT a single node (~0.92) — the R27 second instance.
TCP/IP DEFEATED the rival architectures OSI + X.25 in the protocol wars (~1990-95) (~0.88).
The Web (Berners-Lee, CERN, 1989-91) is the dominant harvest application that drove mass adoption (~0.95).
frontier: THE PACKET-SWITCHING PRIORITY DISPUTE — who 'invented' it: Kleinrock's contested claim vs the historians'/Hall-of-Fame Baran+Davies attribution (Davies 2001 rebuttal; McKenzie; Taylor). A live, bitter dispute (~0.5 on Kleinrock's origin claim; ~0.9 on the Baran/Davies attribution). The specimen's deepest frontier root.

THE CONTESTED GENEALOGY of 'the Internet' — is the child the internetworking WELD (this render) or is it just the ARPANET grown up (the popular conflation)? The boundary of the child is itself fuzzy (~0.6 that 'ARPANET = the Internet' is wrong-but-popular).

THE WHIG-VS-REVISIONIST historiography of the protocol wars — was TCP/IP's victory inevitable-on-technical-merit (the winners' story) or contingent-and-political (Russell's revisionist thesis: government subsidy + commercialization timing + OSI's self-inflicted committee paralysis)? (~0.5, observer-relative).

THE STRAWMAN-FRAMING of OSI by the winners — Internet engineers 'lampooned OSI as a misguided monstrosity created by clueless European bureaucrats' (Russell); Russell's own 2006 article 'presented OSI as a foil'. The clean 'TCP/IP simply better' rendering is part-constructed (~0.6).
W_B as a SINGLE parent (vs the composite of Kahn's ground rules + datagram + end-to-end) — a lossy projection (~0.7).
fuzzy_layer.core_boundary_locus: The certain-core/frontier boundary does NOT fall horizontally across the trunk (as in QG, where it sinks below the child). Like Manhattan, it runs VERTICALLY ALONGSIDE a solid trunk: the entire main lineage (parents -> seam -> weld -> child -> hardening) is certain core, and the frontier is a thin sheath of (a) the PRIORITY DISPUTE + CONTESTED GENEALOGY beneath/around the parents (who invented what; what the child even is) and (b) the WHIG-VS-REVISIONIST historiography + the OSI strawman hovering beside the consummated child (why it won). The boundary's location is itself the diagnostic: a consummated weld keeps its core all the way up the trunk and pushes the fuzz OUT to attribution (the roots) and historiography (the periphery) — the same geometric inverse of QG's hollow crown that Manhattan showed, with the difference that here BOTH the roots (priority) AND the periphery (historiography) carry fuzz (Manhattan's roots were clean; only its moral periphery was fuzzy).

discrepancies._comment: discrepancy[1] — the priority dispute (the specimen's deepest frontier root).
discrepancies.what: WHO invented packet-switching? Kleinrock has claimed priority (and to have convinced Roberts to adopt it); Donald Davies (posthumously, 2001) denied Kleinrock's early-1960s work was about packet-switching ('I can find no evidence that he understood the principles of packet switching'); Alex McKenzie ('nothing in the entire 1964 book...alludes to packetization'); Bob Taylor ('the Kleinrock-Roberts claims are not believed'). Historians + the US National Inventors Hall of Fame credit Baran AND Davies, independently. Kleinrock (2023) acknowledged the early work was about MESSAGE switching.

Recorded via graded parent-confidence (Kleinrock's packet-switching carrier-strength 0.35) + this row, NOT via weld.reattribution (it is a dispute over CREDIT for a parent, not a structural re-welding). Notably the dispute 'has affected sources on the topic, creating methodological challenges in the historiography' — the dispute contaminates the record itself.

discrepancies._comment: discrepancy[2] — the contested genealogy of the child itself.
discrepancies.what: WHAT is 'the Internet'? The popular narrative conflates it with the ARPANET ('the ARPANET became the Internet'). This render distinguishes them: the ARPANET is a PARENT-SUBSTRATE (one packet network), and the CHILD is the INTERNETWORKING layer (TCP/IP, the network-of-networks) that federates many networks — which is why the ARPANET could be decommissioned (1990) while the Internet grew. The boundary of the child is itself contested.
discrepancies.why_interesting: A framework-vs-record tension about node IDENTITY: the framework needs the child to be the WELD'S output (internetworking), but the popular record draws the child boundary around the substrate (the ARPANET). Recorded by making the ARPANET a relation:influence relative (not the child, not a rival). Echoes Manhattan's 'is the child the device or the nuclear order' straddle and Keynesian's 'what is Keynesianism' instability — but here the instability is DEFINITIONAL (what counts), not diachronic.
discrepancies.confidence_impact: Holds 'the child = the internetworking weld' at ~0.85; the popular 'ARPANET = the Internet' conflation at ~0.6 (wrong-but-widespread). Child existence unaffected (~0.92).

'History is written by the winners.'

discrepancies._comment: discrepancy[5] — rival-lifecycle-coupling (the SPECIMEN'S OTHER CHIEF GRADUATION DATUM: the second instance of R23).
discrepancies.what: RIVAL-LIFECYCLE-COUPLING: the protocol wars are a case where one architecture's RISE IS another's FALL. GOSIP mandates + ISO backing PULLED OSI/X.25 while SQUEEZING TCP/IP (1985-88); then NSF commercialization (1992-95) + the Web + UNIX-bundling PULLED TCP/IP while OSI/X.25 COLLAPSED. The deepest instance: France's PTT KILLED its own datagram pioneer (CYCLADES, defunded 1978) to back the connection-oriented Minitel/Transpac — and the datagram CYCLADES pioneered then won globally as IP, while Minitel was eventually shut down (2012). One lineage suppressed the winning idea at home and lost to it abroad.

Deep learning's R23 instance was 'connectionism's winter = symbolic AI's spring' (anti-correlated fortunes). HERE it is 'TCP/IP's rise = OSI/X.25/Minitel's fall', explicitly mediated by lineage-relative forcing (GOSIP, commercialization). TWO independent instances (deep learning + the Internet) of a signed rival-lifecycle coupling -> R23 GRADUATES (ready to fold). Also proposes (in weld_type) a companion 'rival-coupled-weld' vocabulary term BEFORE use, per §6 item 7. -> motivates folding R23.

forcing_events._comment: (D4) the EXOGENOUS-FORCING 'weather' layer — FIRST-CLASS and load-bearing here (TRIPLE-attesting D4 with Manhattan + Keynesian). Two distinctive features: (1) a SLOW, multi-stage forcing (Cold War at the start, deregulation at the end) vs Manhattan's single fast war-pull; (2) LINEAGE-RELATIVE direction is everywhere (the protocol wars) — GOSIP/ISO mandates PULL OSI while SQUEEZING TCP/IP, then NSF commercialization inverts it. The R20 (per-target direction) machinery — already ratified — is used heavily.
forcing_events.name: Sputnik / the Cold War (1957) -> ARPA created (1958)
forcing_events.mechanism: The Soviet launch of Sputnik (4 Oct 1957) triggered a Cold-War technological-prestige panic; Eisenhower created ARPA (Feb 1958) to fund high-risk defense research. ARPA -> IPTO -> the ARPANET is the root of the whole cascade. The Cold-War PULL that brought the welding institution into existence (the slow analogue of Manhattan's WWII pull). Baran's survivable-network work was directly Cold-War-motivated (surviving a nuclear first strike).

forcing_events.name: Sustained DARPA/DoD research funding (the ARPANET program)
forcing_events.mechanism: Defense funding built the ARPANET testbed (1969), paid Cerf-Kahn's internetworking program (1973-83), and mandated the 1983 flag day. Without a patient, deep-pocketed state patron with no near-term ROI demand, the open-architecture weld would not have been built + tested at scale. The state-funding PULL (TRIPLE-attesting the D2/D4 government-as-carrier finding with Manhattan + Keynesian).

forcing_events.name: Government OSI mandates (GOSIP) + ISO backing — the rival-lineage pull/squeeze
forcing_events.mechanism: The 1985 US National Research Council recommended migrating FROM TCP/IP TO OSI; the 1988 Commerce Department mandated OSI compliance for federal purchases after Aug 1990 (GOSIP); European governments tied funding to OSI. This PULLED the OSI/X.25 lineage (mandates, investment, the belief it was 'inevitable') while SQUEEZING TCP/IP (officially slated for replacement). LINEAGE-RELATIVE direction (R20, ratified): the SAME policy pulled one lineage and squeezed its rival.
forcing_events._veridicality_note: (R21 graduation datum) The OSI-inevitability belief was a real institutional FORCE (it drove the NRC recommendation + GOSIP + a decade of investment) with a FALSE object — OSI-at-scale never shipped ('OSI is now inevitable' — Metcalfe 1989, proved wrong by 1995). This is the SECOND independent instance of Manhattan's phantom-forcing (real force, false object) -> R21 graduates. A forcing_events.veridical flag would record: ~0.85 the belief drove real forcing; ~0.85 the object was a phantom.

forcing_events.name: France's PTT defunds CYCLADES in favor of Minitel/Transpac
forcing_events.mechanism: The French telecom monopoly (DGT) chose the connection-oriented Transpac/Minitel over Pouzin's connectionless CYCLADES, cut CYCLADES' funding (1978); the network went offline (1981). LINEAGE-RELATIVE (R20): SQUEEZED the datagram pioneer (kill) while PULLING the virtual-circuit rival (Minitel). THE DEEPEST RIVAL-COUPLING IRONY: the datagram CYCLADES pioneered survived into TCP/IP and WON globally; Minitel was eventually shut down (2012). A patron that EXTINGUISHED its own winning lineage (the inverse of a flame-keeper — bears on R29, see discrepancies[6]).
forcing_events._lineage_relative_note: (R20, ratified; + R23 graduation datum) the single best rival-lifecycle-coupling datum: the state's pull on one lineage (Minitel) WAS the squeeze on its rival (CYCLADES), and the suppressed idea (datagram) later defeated the favored one. Feeds the DEFERRED R23 second instance.

forcing_events.name: NSF commercialization / deregulation (lifting the commercial-traffic ban; backbone retirement)
forcing_events.mechanism: The NSF lifted the Acceptable Use Policy's ban on commercial traffic (1991-92) and retired the NSFNET backbone (30 Apr 1995), handing the Internet to commercial ISPs. This DEREGULATION PULL accelerated TCP/IP to global dominance (free + available + already-deployed) while SQUEEZING the now-pointless OSI/X.25 mandates to death (GOSIP dropped OSI 1994-95). LINEAGE-RELATIVE (R20): the deregulation that pulled TCP/IP was the same event that killed OSI's regulatory backing. The DEREGULATION half of the brief's 'Cold-War + deregulation' double forcing.

forcing_events.name: The World Wide Web (Berners-Lee/CERN, 1989-91; public domain 1993) — the killer-harvest pull
forcing_events.mechanism: The Web gave the Internet a mass-market application that ran ONLY on TCP/IP; its explosive growth (and CERN's 1993 royalty-free release) made TCP/IP the obvious universal choice and rendered the OSI debate moot. A harvest that fed back as a FORCING PULL on its own parent-child — the killer argument that ended the protocol wars. (Recorded as forcing because it acted on the WELD's victory, beyond being a descendant.)
